messages.subject: New to tidyLPA, mclust, and Mplus: a few questions from a newbie
messages.subject_clean: New to tidyLPA, mclust, and Mplus: a few questions from a newbie
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
First off, I'm very happy to see an updated version of tidyLPA and appreciate the work that went into it. Statistically, I have a strong understanding of LPA. But, I am relatively (and regrettably) late to adopting R, so this is a steep learning curve. As such, I have a few questions where I could use some help. My apologies in advance for my naivete:

1. Is mclust effectively integrated into tidyLPA? Would there be any advantage to utilizing both mclust and tidyLPA separately?
2. I'm not sure if this is the correct phrasing, but it appears that tidyLPA can be implemented with Mplus using MplusAutomation. Is this a fair statement?
3. What is the advantage of using tidyLPA and Mplus? Most of the papers I've read conducting LPA have used Mplus. As I learn R, I'm concerned about becoming overwhelmed by also having to learn Mplus. I guess that is at the core of my question regarding using both.
4. I am submitting a grant and am wondering if it is worth budgeting in Mplus, which will probably be contingent to responses to the above questions.
5. Relatedly, this is a a project I'm working on with another institution who does not have Mplus but has R. Would utilizing Mplus preclude easily sharing files with this other site, or can tidyLPA in R still be used to easily share data (which goes back to question 3)?

Again, I apologize for the poorly worded questions that may lead to more confusion, but it's the technical aspect of running LPA within software packages that is new to me, not the conceptual and statistical underpinnings of LPA.

Thanks in advance,
Dalin

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm an Undergraduate Psychology student using the tinyLPA package for my Honours Thesis. I would like to ask if it's possible to generate a diagram or statistics of this sort after the LPA is conducted.

These diagrams show the probability of an assigned group in the other groups, as taken from McLaughlin, T. W., Snyder, P. A., & Algina, J. (2015). Characterizing early childhood disabilities in a nationally representative sample using functional profiles. Exceptional Children, 81(4), 471-488. I understand that this previous photo is taken from research which utilised LCA, but I was wondering if a similar table can be created using the data generated.

thank you for your time and patience.
